test_focus: per-prompt routing — classify the USER PROMPT (not just the agent profile) and override the injection wrapper style per-call. The Phase 14 outlier (legacy-deletion at 55% treatment-win on a 'technical' agent) strongly suggested a 'decision-shaped technical prompt' class that would benefit from creative routing.
tester: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context), live as the developer

module_changes: bog_agents_cli/dreamscape/imagination.py — _route_style_for_request() + style_override path in _build_injection_body() + per-call routing in _maybe_inject()
bog_agents_cli/agent.py — the mechanism is shipped but NOT auto-enabled (defaults to False) given Phase 17 validation's ambiguous-to-negative result

validation_experiment_design.scenario_selection: the most decision-shaped Phase 14 scenarios (legacy-deletion 55%, refactor-decision 25%) + a calibration control (retry-under-load 10% in P14, expected to KEEP neutral wrapper)

per_scenario.prompt_classified_as: creative (UNEXPECTED — surface keyword 'designing' triggered creative classification despite my categorizing it as engineering)

implications: **The routing MECHANISM works as designed.** All 3 scenarios got correctly classified (all triggered the dreams wrapper). The decision-pattern detection fires correctly; the prompt classification fires correctly.

**The EFFECTIVENESS is ambiguous-to-negative.** On 2 of 3 scenarios the dreams wrapper underperformed the neutral wrapper from Phase 16. On the third (refactor-decision) it tied. None showed the Phase 11 creative-prompt magic (~79% win rate) we hoped per-prompt routing would unlock on engineering agents.

**Hypothesis: the AGENT VOICE matters more than the wrapper at the call level.** An engineering-profiled agent's voice is engineering. Forcing it to receive a dreams-style injection ('You appear to be stuck. Here is some imagination.') for a decision-shaped prompt doesn't bring the creative-agent magic because the agent itself isn't creative. The Phase 11 win rate came from creative agents getting dreams wrapper — both halves aligned.

**Surprise: the classifier triggered 'creative' on retry-under-load** because 'designing' is a creative keyword. That's a reasonable classification ('I'm designing the retry policy' IS partly a design question) but it shows the keyword-only approach is sometimes too eager.

**Confidence intervals overlap.** P16 legacy-deletion CI [62%, 96%] overlaps with P17 [42%, 85%]; P16 retry-under-load CI [36%, 80%] overlaps with P17 [15%, 58%]. At N=15 we can't statistically distinguish routed vs unrouted. Phase 17's signal is directional (slightly worse on average) but not conclusive.

**Decision: ship the mechanism, DON'T auto-enable.** ImaginationConfig.use_prompt_routing defaults to False. agent.py does NOT enable it for engineering agents. The knob is preserved for future research (Phase 19+) and power-users who want to A/B test on their own workloads.
what_actually_landed: Per-prompt routing mechanism (classify_prompt_domain, _has_decision_signal, style override path)
7 unit tests covering classifier behavior and middleware integration
Agent.py preserves the AGENT-level routing from Phase 11/12 — does not auto-enable per-prompt routing
Phase 17 documentation honestly reporting the ambiguous validation finding

feature_verdicts.per_prompt_routing_mechanism: sings — classifier + middleware integration work correctly
feature_verdicts.per_prompt_routing_effectiveness_on_engi: ambiguous-to-negative — does not reliably improve outcomes
feature_verdicts.shipping_decision: ship the knob, keep it off by default. Engineering agents continue using neutral wrapper for all prompts (Phase 16 validated).
feature_verdicts.decision_pattern_detection: works — fires on intended patterns. The 'designing' keyword overlap with creative-vocabulary is a known false positive.

known_limitations: Per-prompt routing is shipped as a non-default knob. Users can opt in but defaults preserve the validated agent-level routing.
N=15 per scenario, 3 scenarios — insufficient to declare a real negative effect. The CIs overlap with the baseline. A definitive verdict would need N=30+ per scenario.
The keyword classifier sometimes triggers 'creative' on debatable cases ('designing the retry policy' → creative is debatable). A future LLM-classifier fallback (Phase 19) would handle these nuances.
We tested only engineering→creative override. The reverse (creative agent asked a technical question) wasn't tested but is implied by symmetry.
verdict: MIXED — mechanism ships clean (and may be useful for power-users), but per-prompt routing is NOT a default enabled feature. Phase 16's data already validated the agent-level routing as the load-bearing decision; per-prompt is a refinement that didn't pay off at this N.
next_steps: Phase 19 (suggested): LLM-classifier fallback for the long tail of profiles that the keyword classifier returns 'general' on. Could also be used to validate the per-prompt classifier's edge cases ('designing the retry policy').
Phase 20 (suggested): N=30 per-scenario re-run of Phase 17 validation. The current N=15 result is suggestive but not definitive.

Phase 21 (suggested): instead of toggling the WRAPPER per-prompt, toggle the SEED ARCHIVE per-prompt — engineering-craft archive for engineering-shaped questions, broader archive for decision-shaped ones. This is content-level routing rather than wrapper-level routing.
